q: 1. U-shaped pieces made of wrought iron with pointed ends which are used to connect the members are known as ..........
explain: In carpentry, 'dogs' are U-shaped iron fastners used to hold large timber members together during construction or in heavy trusses.

q: 2. A carpentry tools used for making holes is ..........
explain: A gimlet is a hand tool with a screw-tip and a cross-handle used specifically for boring small holes in wood.

q: 3. A window provided on a pitched roof parallel and slightly above the sloping roof surface is known as ..........
explain: Unlike a dormer, a sky light is installed parallel to the roof slope to bring natural light directly into the room below.

q: 4. A window with a fixed glass provided on the flat roof is known as ..........
explain: A lantern window is a glass-walled structure built over an opening in a flat roof to provide extra light and ventilation.

q: 5. The members laid horizontally to support the common rafters and to transmit the load to the trusses walls are called as
explain: Purlins are horizontal beams that span between trusses to support the roof rafters or sheeting.

q: 6. A small wooden block hinged on the post outside the door is known as ..........
explain: A cleat is a small block of wood or metal used to secure a door or provide a stop/grip for a closing mechanism.

q: 7. The short piece of timber bolted to the rafters of a roof truss fixing the purlins in position are named as
explain: Cleats are small blocks used to prevent purlins from sliding or tilting on the rafters.

q: 8. The window projecting beyond the main external wall is ..........
explain: Bay windows project outward from the main wall, increasing the floor area of the room and providing a wide view.

q: 9. For a span ranging in between 3.5 m to 4.5 m the most suitable type of roof is
explain: A couple-close roof adds a horizontal tie to prevent the rafters from spreading, making it suitable for mid-range spans.

q: 10. The maximum allowable deflection of a timber beam supporting a roof of span L is ..........
explain: According to standard structural codes, the deflection of a beam should not exceed 1/360 of the span to prevent cracking of finishes.

q: 11. For a span ranging in between 6 m to 9 m, the most suitable type of pitched roof is
explain: The King Post truss is the most efficient design for spans up to 9 meters.

q: 12. The timber sections of width more than 5 cm and thickness less than 5 cm are known as ..........
explain: Scantlings refer to timber cut to standard sizes with specific dimensions; usually, they are smaller pieces of wood.

q: 13. The inclined braces used in a truss to prevent the sagging of the principal rafters are called as
explain: Struts are compression members in a truss that support the principal rafters and prevent them from bending.

q: 14. The projections of the heads or sills of door or window are called ..........
explain: Horns are the horizontal projections of the head and sill of a frame which are embedded into the masonry to secure the frame.

q: 15. The projected portion of the tread (which is usually rounded) beyond the face of the riser is
explain: This is a repeat of the definition for nosing; it enhances the effective width of the tread.

q: 16. A vertical member supporting the hand rail is known as
explain: Balusters are the smaller vertical members that support the handrail and fill the space between the tread and the rail.

q: 17. In domestic buildings, the sufficient widths of the stair is about
explain: For residential or domestic buildings, a width of 0.9m (approx. 3 feet) is considered sufficient for comfortable movement.

q: 18. The normal tread length varies between
explain: A tread length (going) of 25cm to 30cm ensures the full foot has enough surface area to land safely.

q: 19. A stair in which all the steps are winders is
explain: In a spiral stair, all steps radiate from a central post and are tapered (winders).

q: 20. A stair which changes its direction by 180° is
explain: Half-turn stairs, such as dog-legged stairs, involve two flights that reverse direction by 180 degrees.

q: 21. Dog-legged stair is a
explain: The dog-legged stair is the most common type of half-turn stair where the two flights are contiguous with no well between them.

q: 22. How many treads would be there in a straight stair connecting two floors with height difference of 3.6 m? The rise is 15 cm.
explain: Total risers = 360/15 = 24. Since treads = Risers - 1 for a single flight, the answer is 23.

q: 23. How many treads would be there in a dog-legged stair connecting two floor with a height difference of 3.6 m? The rise of the steps is 15 cm.
explain: In a dog-legged stair with two flights, each flight has 12 risers and 11 treads. Total treads = 11 + 11 = 22.

q: 24. A roof which slopes in all four directions and having flat top is known as
explain: A deck roof is similar to a hip roof but the top portion is kept flat for use as a terrace.

q: 25. The horizontal wooden or steel members which support the common rafter in a truss are called
explain: Purlins are horizontal members spanning between trusses to support the rafters or roofing sheets.

q: 26. Queen-post trusses are used when the span is
explain: Queen post trusses are economical and suitable for spans ranging from 8 to 12 meters.

q: 27. A screw with a square head is known as ..........
explain: Coach screws (or lag bolts) have square or hexagonal heads and are designed to be tightened with a wrench for heavy timber joints.

q: 28. Joining two wooden members at an angle is known as
explain: Mitring is the process of joining two pieces of wood at an angle, usually 45 degrees, to form a corner.

q: 29. In doors and windows, style is
options: the vertical member of the frame
the vertical member of the shutter
the member which divides the frame into two vertical portions
explain: Styles are the outermost vertical members of a door or window shutter.

q: 30. The horizontal members of the shutter of a door or window are called
explain: Rails are the horizontal structural members of a shutter, such as top, lock, and bottom rails.

q: 31. The normal height of the door in residential buildings
explain: A standard door height for residential buildings is typically 2.0 meters (approx 6'7").

q: 32. A window designated as 10 WS 15 means ..........
options: a fixed window of size 1 m x 1.5 m
a fixed window of size 0.5 m x 0.75 m
a single shuttered window of size 1 m x 1.5 m
a double shuttered window of size 1 m x 1.5 m
explain: 10 represents width in decimeters (1m), WS stands for Window with Double Shutters, and 15 is the height (1.5m).

q: 33. The thickness of shutter of the door generally does not exceed
explain: Standard internal wooden door shutters are usually 30mm thick.

q: 34. In the battened and ledged door, the vertical wooden boards are called
explain: Battens are the vertical boards; they are secured by horizontal ledges.

q: 35. The type of door used when good ventilation is required in the room and at the same time privacy is maintained
explain: Louvered doors have slanted slats that allow air through while obstructing direct vision.

q: 36. A cut made in the frame of a door to receive the shutter is known as ..........
explain: A rebate is a stepped rectangular recess cut into the edge of a frame to allow the door shutter to sit flush within it.

q: 37. The line of intersection of the surfaces of a sloping roof forming an external angle exceeding 180°, is
explain: A hip is the external angle formed by the intersection of two sloping roof surfaces.

q: 38. The width of jamb is ..........
explain: In standard timber door frames, the width of the jamb (the vertical side member) typically ranges between 76 mm and 114 mm.

q: 39. The depth of jamb is ..........
explain: The depth or thickness of the jamb for a standard door frame generally matches the width, falling in the range of 76 mm to 114 mm.

q: 40. In wooden stairs the thickness of the member used as tread is generally ..........
explain: To provide sufficient structural strength for foot traffic, the horizontal part of the step (tread) in timber stairs is usually 38 mm thick.

q: 41. While the depth of the rebate equals the thickness of the door shutter, the width of the rebate is usually ..........
explain: The rebate depth matches the door thickness (e.g., 30-40mm), but the width (the overlap) is usually about 12 mm.

q: 42. In a paneled door, the rails fixed in between the lock rail and top rail are known as ..........
explain: The frieze rail is the intermediate horizontal member located between the top rail and the lock rail.

q: 43. The most suitable type of door for air-conditioned rooms ..........
explain: Revolving doors minimize the exchange of air between the interior and exterior, making them highly efficient for climate control.

q: 44. The number of steps in a flight should not be less than ..........
explain: A flight of stairs should have at least 3 steps to be easily recognized as a change in level, preventing tripping hazards.

q: 45. The number of steps in an ordinary flight shall not be more than ..........
explain: A flight is generally limited to 12 steps to prevent excessive fatigue for the user before reaching a landing.

q: 46. The extreme vertical support to the hand railing provided at the top and bottom of a flight is known as ..........
explain: The newel post is the heavy vertical post at the start and end of a staircase that anchors the handrail.

q: 47. The under surface of a stair is known as ..........
explain: The soffit refers to the visible underside of any structural element, including the underside of a staircase.

q: 48. The additional support given to the nosing in wooden stair is known as ..........
explain: A scotia is a decorative moulding placed under the nosing of a tread to provide additional support and a finished look.

q: 49. In a stair, the ratio of the vertical distance covered to the horizontal distance occupied by the flight is called ..........
explain: The pitch (or slope) of a stair is the angle between the line of nosings and the horizontal plane.

q: 50. The vertical intermediate support to the hand railing is known as ..........
explain: Balusters are the smaller vertical members that support the handrail and are spaced along the treads.
